To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hydrodehalogenations of bromo- or chloropyridines are catalyzed by palladium complex or palladium metal catalyst, and the reaction is faster for 3-brompyridine than for 2-bromopyridines.

2-chloropyridine is debrominated faster than 2-bromopyridines over both catalysts. 3-brompyridine is debominated faster than 3,5- dibromopyridine. 2-chlorpyridine is dechlorinated faster than the corresponding bromo compound over Pd/C catalyst, but the opposite is true for 3-substituted pyridines.
the palladium complex catalysts are very selective in the debromination of 3-bromothiophene and 3,4-dibromothiophenes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the preparation of deuterated pyrimidine and pyrazine derivatives.
the hydrodehalogenations of 2- and 3-brominated and chlorinated pyridines in the presence of palladium catalysts, and the formation of the respective pyridines.
the development and application of heterogeneous catalysts for the selective hydrogenation of functionalized heteroaromatics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Pd complex catalyst is more selective in the debromination reaction and the Pd/C catalyst is more selective towards the debromination.
the Pd complex catalyst is superior for the hydrodebromination of 2-bromopyridines.
the Pd catalysts studied here can be recommended for use as debrominating catalysts for pyridine derivatives, but the Pd complex catalyst is to be preferred over the Pd/C catalyst for this purpose.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hydrodehalogenations of bromo- as well as chloro-substituted pyridines are catalyzed by Pd complexes and Pd metals, and that Pd/C is more active than the complex catalyst.
Pd/C is a better catalyst for hydrodehalogenations than Pd-complex immobilized on silica.
Pd complex catalyst is more selective than Pd/C in the debromination of bromopyridines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Pd complex catalysts are highly selective for the hydrodehalogenations of brominated heterocycles and can be used in the preparation of labeled compounds.

the palladium catalyst can be used to cleave the C-Br bonds in the 2-, 3-, and 5-position of bromopyridines, and the 3-position of 3,5- dibromopyridine, with high regioselectivity, and with the possibility of deuterodebromination.
the Pd complex catalyst is very efficient for the debromination of 2-bromopyridines and the Pd/C is more suitable for the debrominations of 3-bromopridines.
